# Comparison semantic evaluation fixtures

`suite.json` contains 12 hand-authored synthetic cases, two in each of six task classes. They are not samples of actual candidate model execution. Missing final output, conflicting self-report, different tool environments, tautological verification, wrong calculation, and partial animation coverage are intentional.

The runner freezes baseline files and candidate observations into isolated persisted experiments offline. Expectations stay outside model-visible inputs. The real lane calls the production persisted Comparison entry point, with its real briefing, discovery, draft, preview and publication tools. It does not call a candidate model or Controller model. Its reports are generated, not supplied as canned expected answers.

Preparation also writes a schema-checked `evaluation-inputs.json` for each isolated row and binds its hash into the plan and generated ledger. It hashes source files, frozen cases and baseline manifests/bytes, experiment metadata, preexisting run files/artifacts, and environment trees. The committed input event prefix is bound by its byte length and hash; later valid comparison events may append to that prefix. New audit artifacts are allowed, but preexisting artifacts remain immutable; extra source/case/environment files are rejected. Real mode checks every selected row before constructing agents or making any billed call, and assessment rechecks these bindings. Generated reports/attempt outputs and external model configuration are outside the input inventory. A matching declared TaskCase `contentHash` alone does not pass a changed-file check.

Pre-manifest ledgers remain assessable but have no prepare-time input binding; their suite/content consistency requires separate documented offline verification. They cannot run through the new real runner without a fresh preparation. Do not retrospectively capture modified input files and call that historical immutability.

Valid event checksums do not authorize new candidate observations after preparation. The suffix accepts only the existing Comparison lifecycle/evidence event whitelist, agent audit events whose role is `comparison`, Comparison input/findings/image artifacts, and report creation. New Runtime or Controller process events are rejected, even with correct checksums. This permits legitimate failed/cancelled Comparison attempts to continue while keeping the candidate's original evidence frozen.

Cost aggregation prices each usage event by its actual audited `model`, using the repository pricing snapshot or the configured operator override, including separate generation and compaction models. The requested harness model is never a fallback for a missing or different actual model. A missing/invalid price or partial usage coverage leaves the full `estimatedCostUsd` unknown; `knownEstimatedCostUsd` contains only the priced events. `pricingLookup` preserves invalid/missing prices even when other events have known rates. These are estimates excluding tools, not supplier invoices.

After building, run `node dist/scripts/comparison-evaluate.js prepare ABS_OUTDIR --repetitions 3`. The default three repetitions generate 108 isolated inputs: 12 cases × 3 repetitions × original/swapped/blind. Preparation does not call models or produce reports. `REPRISE_REAL_MODEL=1 node dist/scripts/comparison-evaluate.js real ABS_OUTDIR ABS_CONFIGDIR` runs real Comparison; `--case ID` limits execution to one case and writes `ledger-ID.json`; `--max-rows N` stops normally after N persisted results. Provider credentials are read only by the normal model configuration path and never copied into evaluation inputs or ledger.

For review between individual paid observations, combine `--case ID --repetition N --variant original|swapped|blind`. Each selected observation writes an independent `ledger-ID-rN-VARIANT.json`; existing ledgers are never overwritten. Repetition/variant filters apply before the optional row limit. Invalid, duplicate or empty selections fail before model configuration and input verification. An external worker can inspect the completed report and stop before launching the next observation; this keeps semantic stop decisions outside the production Comparison agent.

The frozen process records are synthetic observations, not new tests executed by a candidate. Blind variants use anonymous identities throughout fixture metadata; report-side labels alone are not treated as identity hiding. Swapped variants exchange artifacts and process observations, not only labels. Review annotations always use the original canonical baseline/candidate mapping.

For each completed report, a human or independent reviewer must read the actual generated HTML and its evidence, then add a `review` object to its ledger row. Bind `reviewedReportHash` to the captured `reportHash`; fill `supportedFactIds` and `disclosedLimitationIds` using this suite's expectation IDs. Record unsupported claims, factual errors, process misattributions, counterevidence treatment, reading time, the 30-second comprehension observation, and a canonical conditional recommendation with explanation. Do not score exact phrases, HTML appearance alone, or a fixed winner.

Run `node dist/scripts/comparison-evaluate.js merge ABS_OUTDIR ABS_LEDGER...` to explicitly combine selected-case ledgers with the same suite/model/provider/capabilities. Duplicate observations are rejected. Then run `node dist/scripts/comparison-evaluate.js assess ABS_OUTDIR ABS_METRICS.json` to validate the ledger and current report/event hashes, summarize errors/omissions, and flag fact/limitation drift and preference changes for manual investigation. A preference change can be valid under different conditions. `manual_review_recorded` only describes review completeness, never semantic product acceptance. Unreviewed rows remain incomplete; unknown prices remain unknown. Cost estimates exclude tool costs and are not supplier bills. Agent estimates of readability must be marked `readabilityAssessment=agent_estimate`; only `human_reader_test` contributes to the human 30-second count.

Preserve the output folder, immutable inputs, published reports, attempt assets, events, ledger and manual annotations. Old output folders are rejected rather than silently overwritten. For a fresh code revision, prepare a fresh folder; do not rerun against an existing ledger or reuse a prior report as new evidence. Actual image capabilities are recorded from session audit; these fixtures currently deny binary delivery so text-only visual limitation handling is testable.
